body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-30 against `cwn-local` (published `:dev` image, digest parity with the canary),
mobile project, 390x844.

`frontend/e2e/my-library.spec.ts` "adding an unowned book to a shelf establishes membership first"
fails its axe gate on mobile:

    target-size: All touch targets must be 24px large, or leave sufficient space

    a[href="/app/tags/161"]  smallest space 46.8px by 9.7px, should be at least 24px by 24px
    a[href$="tags/6"]        smallest space 141.7px by 9.7px, should be at least 24px by 24px
    "Target has insufficient size because it is PARTIALLY OBSCURED"

## The obvious reading is wrong

The tag links are not undersized. Measured directly on a book detail page at the same viewport:

    tag link height   28.6px      (SC 2.5.8 floor is 24px)
    .tags row gap     4px
    row tops          579.8 -> 612.4     (579.8 + 28.6 = 608.4; no overlap)

Controls: book detail at 390x844 with nothing open scans axe-CLEAN; the same page with the
add-to-shelf popover open on a book whose tags do not sit under the panel also scans CLEAN. So the
violation is not a property of the tag chips and not a property of the page.

## What it actually is

The failure screenshot shows the add-to-shelf popover OPEN and overlapping the controls beneath it
— an action button is visibly clipped to "...er" behind the panel, and the tags row sits at its
lower edge. The page behind the popover is not inert, so those covered controls remain in the hit
test and in the accessibility tree. Axe measures each target's UNOBSCURED area, finds ~9.7px of
vertical space, and correctly reports SC 2.5.8.

So the defect is: **an open popover covers live, still-interactive controls.** That is a real
usability and accessibility problem independent of the axe rule — a tap near the panel edge can
activate something the user cannot see, and assistive tech can still reach it.

## Why it matters beyond the failing test

This is the same family as the coarse-pointer disclosure defect (#2028): an element that is
visually covered but not actually disarmed. Hiding or covering a control does not disable it.

The suite already knows the correct pattern — `a11y.spec.ts` asserts "mobile: closed drawer is
inert; open traps focus and Escape closes" for the navigation drawer. The shelf popover does not
follow it.

## Fix direction (not yet decided)

Either make the popover a proper modal surface (mark the rest of the page `inert` while open, trap
focus, Escape to close, matching the drawer), or lay it out so it cannot overlap interactive
content. The first matches the established pattern in this codebase.

Done-condition for whoever takes it: the mobile axe gate on that spec must go from RED to GREEN,
and a test must assert the background is genuinely inert while the popover is open — not merely
that the popover renders.
title: Add-to-shelf popover overlays live controls without making them inert, failing SC 2.5.8 on mobile
